title: Redraw the boot bloom so the player rises from behind the petals, with before-and-after animations to review
tier_reason: Changes the title-screen animation every player sees on boot, and the look of it is Daniel's taste to settle — he asked to review the before and after himself.
ask: Fix the boot bloom so she isn't drawn through the closed bud, and bring me the before and after animations with the results.
first_action: Edit tools/experiments/vfx_sunflower_bloom.py to add closed-to-open bud frames and raise her from behind the petals into the standing pose, clipped so nothing of her shows below the petals while she is low; keep the existing sunflower_bloom.gif aside as the before, re-export via export_anim_loop.py to assets/anim/sunflower_bloom/, and attach the before gif, the revised gif and the three capture_boot_bloom.tscn moments to the result.
source_message: Please show me an animation of the before and after attached to the results that I'll review.  The new animation will also be parameterized and viewable as a new version of the previous version, in the animation lab, right?
result: I'll wait for that to notify me rather than poll further.

check.summary: The redraw landed and works: frame 0 is now a sealed bud and she rises out of it with nothing showing below the reveal line, and the old loop is kept as a before set; but the three in-game captures were never made, and the reply reports nothing at all, so the before-and-after Daniel asked to be brought to him has not been brought.

findings.what: The reply is not a report. It says 'I'll wait for that to notify me' and nothing else: no before, no after, no captures, no description of what changed. Daniel asked for the animations with the results; none were attached.
findings.fix: Replace with a short report that attaches sunflower_bloom_before/sunflower_bloom.gif and sunflower_bloom/sunflower_bloom.gif and says in one line what the two new dials (sink, bud_w) do.

findings.what: The three capture_boot_bloom.tscn moments were not produced; tools/boot_bloom_shots/ is empty. That capture needs a display, which the headless worker did not have.
findings.fix: Run `godot --path . res://tools/capture_boot_bloom.tscn` on the desktop and attach the three PNGs before this reaches Daniel.

findings.what: The bud reads as a flat green box, not a bud, and it stays drawn as a green bar over the flower for frames 3 to 5 while the petals are already fanned open around it (open=7 keeps it until frame 6).
findings.fix: Retire the bud when the petals pass roughly half open, or shrink its width with (1 - p), so the open disc is not fighting a green rectangle; then re-export and regenerate the before/after.

findings.what: Design doc check: the Q-103 entry says the engine's splash is the closed bud, which the new frame 0 now matches better than the old one did. No doc contradicts the change.

follow_ups.title: Put the before and after boot bloom animations on the card
follow_ups.first_action: Render tools/capture_boot_bloom.tscn and tools/capture_boot_fade.tscn on the pre-fix commit and on the current working tree, then attach both strips to the work card so the two sit side by side.
follow_ups.why: He asked for before and after animations and the card reached his verdict without them.

follow_ups.title: Add a test that the player is never drawn in front of a closed bud
follow_ups.first_action: Add a test that boots the bloom sequence and asserts the player's draw order stays behind the petal sprites until the bud opens, wired into tools/test_runner.gd.
follow_ups.why: The same layering mistake can come back silently on the next art change.

follow_ups.title: Make a work card carry its deliverable before it reaches the CEO
follow_ups.first_action: In hq/static/work.js, hold a finished card out of the verdict list when its ask names an artifact (animation, capture, table) and no attachment is present, showing what is missing instead of an accept button.
follow_ups.why: This card let an agent's stray sentence stand in for the result he was promised.

recommend.question: Sign off on the boot bloom now, or once you have seen the two animations?
recommend.answer: Accept the card to start the renders, and hold your look verdict until the before and after are in front of you.
recommend.why: Accepting the fix costs nothing you can't revert, but approving art you haven't seen is the one part of this only you can do.
recommend.instead: Reject outright and make the redraw come back whole — honest, but it throws away a fix that is probably correct.
